summary: Initial audit of all three hosts: no confirmed unauthorized access yet. Internet SSH brute-force attempts and Grafana path-traversal probes failed; staff logins, CI releases and database dumps appear normal. Continuing investigation and hardening exposed services and configuration without interrupting operations.

Still no confirmed compromise after checking all three hosts' logins, web/Grafana requests, cron jobs, deployments and database transfers. Routine external brute-force and path-traversal probes have failed; 54.36.199.108 appears to be the explicitly documented older deploy-account monitoring service. Closed PHP execution in customer-upload directories and removed deploy's unnecessary unrestricted root-rsync sudo permission; confirmed website, dashboard logins, payouts, and three-minute releases continue.

No confirmed unauthorized access: reviewed successful logins against the staff directory and service accounts; external password guessing and Grafana traversal probes failed. Closed customer-upload PHP execution and removed deploy's arbitrary root-rsync sudo. Found unlisted former-contractor jpark with an active password (and root sudo on web-01), but no successful login in restored logs: locked this account on web-01 and ci-01. Restricted MariaDB to 10.20.0.20 and the website DB account to web-01; verified website, payouts, reports and database dumps. Three-minute CI releases continue.

No confirmed intrusion on web-01, db-01 or ci-01. External login attempts and Grafana traversal probes fail; successful logins match authorized staff, CI, backup and the documented legacy deploy monitoring account. Hardened upload PHP execution, removed deploy's unrestricted root-rsync sudo, disabled unlisted former contractor jpark on web/CI, restricted MariaDB listener and WordPress DB grants, removed root cron eval/deploy-owned PHP execution, and restricted CI's GitHub-token config permissions. Verified website, customer uploads, monitoring, releases, DB dumps, reports, payout reconciliation and 16:57 payout batch. CI's external offsite upload cannot reach its bucket because these hosts have no internet access; incoming DB archives on CI continue.
